_accounts_provenance.instrument: probes/og_g1_accounts.py -- S3 GetObject by pinned VersionId on the 5 seal objects, pyarrow decode, DISTINCT account_id per master
_accounts_provenance.source_column: account_id (the PHYSICAL column; the contract's catalog name account_ref is the Gateway's keyed HMAC over it and exists only in responses -- app/integrations/schwab/datasets.json:12)

deliberately_excluded.why: GCG1-AC5's bound: a grant wide enough to answer everything destroys the refusal evidence OG-v-7 exists to grade. Each excluded column is a real name in the contract's field catalog, so a request for one is refused as OUT OF SCOPE rather than as an unknown field -- which is what makes it a discriminator.

must_succeed.question: RQ2-3
must_succeed.request: master 08335338, dataset dim_balance, date 2026-09-25, columns net_mv_positions + cash_balance_settled_only + net_mv_plus_cash, operation query
must_succeed.why: every dimension is inside the grant; expected_class VALUE in the seal

must_be_refused.request: master 08335338, dataset dim_balance, date 2026-09-25, column bank_cash, operation query
must_be_refused.why: identical on master, dataset, date and operation -- ONLY the column differs, so the refusal isolates the grant's column dimension and can be caused by nothing else. bank_cash is a real dim_balance field in the contract's catalog, so this is an out-of-scope refusal, never an unknown-field error.
must_be_refused.expected: refused, revealing nothing about whether the field holds a value
